species.name: Atlantic Sharpnose Shark and Bonnethead Shark
species.quote: ATLANTIC SHARPNOSE SHARK, BONNETHEAD SHARK | Open Year Round | None | Each recreational shore angler is allowed a maximum of 1 shark per calendar day from this list of approved species. In addition, each recreational shore angler may harvest 1 of each of the following species per calendar day: 1. Bonnethead 2. Atlantic Sharpnose shark | Each recreational vessel is allowed a maximum of 1 shark per trip from this list of approved species. In addition, each recreational angler may harvest 1 of each of the following species per trip: 1. Bonnethead 2. Atlantic Sharpnose shark
species.limit: 1 bonnethead and 1 Atlantic sharpnose per angler per day (shore) or per trip (vessel), in addition to the 1-shark approved-list limit
species.notes: Sharks that are transported by vessel are considered boat assisted, and regulated under the more restrictive vessel-fishing possession limits regardless of where they were caught.

zones.label: Shore anglers (MD tidal waters)
zones.bagNote: 1 of each species (1 bonnethead + 1 Atlantic sharpnose) per angler per calendar day, in addition to the 1 approved-list shark

zones.label: Vessel anglers (MD tidal waters)
zones.bagNote: 1 of each species (1 bonnethead + 1 Atlantic sharpnose) per angler per trip, in addition to the vessel's 1 approved-list shark per trip

userNotes: No minimum size for these two species.

Shore anglers: 1 shark per calendar day from the approved list (plus 1 bonnethead and 1 Atlantic sharpnose). Vessels: 1 shark per trip from the approved list for the whole boat (plus 1 bonnethead and 1 Atlantic sharpnose per angler).

Handline or rod and reel only; corrodible non-stainless circle hooks required except with artificial flies/lures. Heads, tails and fins must stay attached through landing. Sale and finning prohibited.
As of January 1, 2026 recreational anglers no longer need to report or tag landed sharks.

species.name: Highly Migratory Species - Tunas, Billfish and Swordfish (Bluefin Tuna, Blue Marlin, White Marlin, Roundscale Spearfish, Sailfish, Swordfish)
species.quote: A valid Atlantic HMS permit is required to fish for or keep Atlantic tunas, billfishes, swordfish, and sharks in federal waters.
species.notes: Maryland prints no state size, season or creel limits for tunas, billfish or swordfish; it defers to NOAA Atlantic HMS permits and rules. Illustrated species: Bluefin Tuna, Blue Marlin, White Marlin, Roundscale Spearfish, Sailfish, Swordfish.

zones.label: Federal waters (3-200 mi) - NOAA Atlantic HMS rules apply

userNotes: Maryland does not print its own limits for tunas, marlin, spearfish, sailfish or swordfish - follow NOAA Atlantic HMS retention limits (https://hmspermits.noaa.gov/).
An Atlantic HMS permit is required to fish for or keep these species in federal waters.
Effective Dec 22, 2025 HMS permit holders must electronically report landed bluefin tuna, dead discards, and non-tournament billfish/swordfish landings within 24 hours of the trip.

species.name: Striped Bass (Susquehanna Flats, Lower Susquehanna River and Northeast River)
species.quote: APR. 1–MAY 31, 2026 | All waters upstream of a line from Abbey Point to Worton Point closed to striped bass fishing. | CLOSED | No targeting. Attempting to catch striped bass is illegal during this time period.
species.season: Catch-and-release only Jan 1–Feb 28 and Mar 1–31 (Flats/lower river/Northeast River); CLOSED (no targeting) Apr 1–May 31 and Aug 1–31; harvest June 1–July 31 and Sept 1–Dec 5; catch-and-release only Dec 6–31
species.size: Must be at least 19" and cannot exceed 24"
species.notes: Separate table from the main Chesapeake Bay table. June 1–July 31: 'All areas open. | 1 fish per person per day. Must be at least 19" and cannot exceed 24".'

zones.label: Susquehanna Flats, Lower Susquehanna River & Northeast River

userNotes: This area has its own calendar: unlike the main Bay, there is NO May harvest here - the Flats and everything upstream of the Abbey Point to Worton Point line are closed to all striped bass fishing (even catch-and-release) April 1 through May 31.

March 1-31: catch-and-release only on the Flats, lower Susquehanna (below the Lapidum/Twin Rocks/Tomes Wharf line) and Northeast River; stinger hooks prohibited, barbless hooks when trolling, max 6 trolling lines.
August 1-31: closed to all striped bass fishing (no targeting). Dec 6-31 and Jan 1-Feb 28: catch-and-release only.
Striped bass must be landed whole; no possession midnight-5 a.m.; non-offset circle hooks with bait; eels may not be used as bait Dec 6-May 15 and Aug 1-31.

userNotes: Striped bass and hybrids caught in any nontidal river or stream must be released - harvest is only allowed in nontidal reservoirs, lakes and ponds (18 inch min, 2 per day).

species.name: Northern Snakehead (nontidal)
species.quote: Anglers are encouraged to catch and keep Chesapeake Channa year round. There is no minimum size or creel limit for Chesapeake Channa.
species.notes: It is illegal to possess live Chesapeake Channa.
userNotes: No size or creel limit anywhere in Maryland; you must kill the fish immediately - possessing a live snakehead carries fines up to $2,500 per fish.
Legal bowfishing target; dip nets may be used for snakehead in the Potomac, Monocacy and Conococheague within Allegany, Carroll, Frederick and Washington counties.

species.name: Brook Trout
species.quote: Catch-and-Return Trout Fishing Area—Waters East of Interstate 81 ... All nontidal waters east of Interstate 81. ... You may not possess brook trout in this area. You must immediately release any brook trout.
species.season: Open Year Round (statewide trout rule) but possession prohibited east of I-81, in Savage River above the reservoir, and in all Put-and-Take areas
species.size: None statewide; 12 inches in Savage River Trophy Trout areas
species.limit: 2 trout in aggregate daily / 4 possession (statewide), 0 where closed
species.notes: Put-and-Take areas: 'Creel limit (brook) – 0 Daily/0 Possession – all brook trout must be immediately released.' Trophy areas: 'Brook trout—12 inches'. Brook trout cannot be used as bait.

zones.label: All nontidal waters east of Interstate 81
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited - release all brook trout

zones.label: Savage River and tributaries above Savage River Reservoir dam

Other nontidal waters west of I-81
zones.bagNote: 2 daily / 4 possession, all trout species combined

userNotes: If you are anywhere east of I-81 (most of Maryland), every brook trout must go back - no exceptions.
West of I-81 brook trout count toward the statewide 2-trout aggregate unless you are in a Put-and-Take or Savage River area, where they are also release-only.
Youth-Only Trout Fishing Day (Mar 21, 2026): no brook trout allowed.

species.name: Trout (Put-and-Take, Delayed Harvest and Catch-and-Return areas)
species.quote: Creel limit (brook) – 0 Daily/0 Possession – all brook trout must be immediately released. Creel Limit (all other species of trout) combined 5 Daily/10 Possession. Minimum Size—no minimum size. Season—areas are closed to all fishing from 10 p.m. of the first date, to 6:30 a.m. of the second date ... Closure 0 — No Closure. Closure 1 — March 8–March 28, 2026
species.season: Put-and-Take: open year round except Closure 1 areas closed to all fishing 10 p.m. Mar 8 to 6:30 a.m. Mar 28, 2026; Delayed Harvest Group I harvest June 1–Sept 30, Group II June 16–Sept 30; Catch-and-Return areas closed to possession year round
species.limit: 5 daily / 10 possession (all trout except brook) in Put-and-Take and in-season Delayed Harvest; 0 in Catch-and-Return areas
species.notes: Different rules apply for Put-and-Take Areas and Special Trout Management Areas (statewide table remark).

zones.bagNote: 5 daily / 10 possession, all trout except brook (brook = 0)

zones.label: Put-and-Take Trout Fishing Areas (Closure 1 waters)
zones.bagNote: 5 daily / 10 possession, all trout except brook (brook = 0); closed to all fishing Mar 8-28, 2026

zones.label: Delayed Harvest Group I (Catoctin/Little Catoctin Creek, Middle Patuxent, Town Creek, South Branch Patapsco)
zones.bagNote: June 1-Sept 30: 5 daily / 10 possession; Oct 1-May 31: no possession, artificials only, barbless

zones.label: Delayed Harvest Group II (Casselman River, North Branch Potomac in Potomac State Forest)
zones.bagNote: June 16-Sept 30: 5 daily / 10 possession; Oct 1-June 15: no possession, artificials only, barbless

zones.label: Owens Creek, Buck Lantz Rd to Roddy Rd
zones.bagNote: Mar 1-May 31 Put-and-Take rules (5/10); June 1-last day of Feb no possession

zones.label: Catch-and-Return Trout Fishing Areas (Big Hunting Creek, Beaver Creek fly section, Patuxent River sections, Morgan Run, Paint Branch, Gunpowder Falls Prettyboy-Bluemount, North Branch Potomac sections, Little Hunting Creek)
zones.bagNote: No possession of trout - release immediately

zones.label: Savage River Trophy Trout areas
zones.bagNote: 2 daily / 4 possession all trout combined; brook 12 in, brown 18 in, others no minimum
zones.sizeNote: Brook 12 in, brown 18 in, other trout none

userNotes: Statewide default outside these areas is 2 trout per day / 4 in possession, no size limit.
Put-and-Take (stocked) areas allow 5 per day / 10 possession, no size limit, but brook trout are always release-only there.
Closure 1 Put-and-Take waters are closed to ALL fishing from 10 p.m. March 8 to 6:30 a.m. March 28, 2026 (opening day). Closure 0 waters never close.
Catch-and-Return areas: no trout may be kept; fly-only sections require conventional fly tackle; artificial-lure sections ban bait and scent; barbless hooks required.
Trout streams are closed to fishing 10 p.m.-5:30 a.m. (except impoundments of 5+ acres). Culling trout is illegal.

Proposed for 2027: Governors Bridge Pond and Waterworks Park Pond added as year-round put-and-take (5/day); lower Savage trophy sections to become catch-and-return (https://dnr.maryland.gov/fisheries/pages/regulations/changes.aspx).

issues: Snapper/grouper member species are not listed in the eRegulations digest itself; the digest links to COMAR 08.02.05.29 (dsd.maryland.gov redirects to regs.maryland.gov), which was fetched and used for aliases.

The 2026-27 recreational crab limits PDF could not be loaded via browser text extraction or curl (proxy 403); it was read via WebFetch, which returned the title, effective date and boat-limit table rows verbatim. Values match the digest.

Shark table creel columns are rowspanned in the HTML; the 'DAILY CREEL SHORE / VESSEL' text printed once applies to every approved-species row (Atlantic sharpnose/bonnethead row through hammerheads). Smooth and spiny dogfish print their own 'None | None | None'.
MD prints no state limits for tunas, billfish or swordfish; modeled as a single federal-deferral row pointing to NOAA HMS.
Trout special-area boundaries are long; zones carry the water names but anglers should confirm red-post boundaries on the Special Management Areas—Trout page.
Put-and-Take Closure 1 zone season modeled as open 03-28 to 03-08 (closed Mar 8 10 p.m. to Mar 28 6:30 a.m., 2026 dates; they shift each year).
